exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, Hong Kong Departure, radar contact. Climb via SID to Flight Level zero nine zero.
exchanges.meaning: Departure establishes radar contact and clears Cathay 251 to climb via the SID to FL090, complying with all published lateral, altitude, and speed constraints.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Climb via SID to Flight Level zero nine zero, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback of the climb-via-SID clearance.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, cancel level restriction, climb to Flight Level one six zero, expedite through Flight Level one zero zero.
exchanges.meaning: Departure cancels the SID level restrictions and orders a climb to FL160, expedited through FL100.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Climb to Flight Level one six zero, cancel level restriction, expediting through Flight Level one zero zero, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback confirming the unrestricted climb to FL160 and expediting through FL100.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, traffic conflict overhead, stop climb at Flight Level one two zero!
exchanges.meaning: The emergency command to stop the climb at FL120 because of conflicting traffic overhead.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Stopping climb at Flight Level one two zero, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback confirming the climb is being arrested at FL120.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, expedite climb through Flight Level one four zero, crossing traffic opposite direction.
exchanges.meaning: Departure orders an expedited climb through FL140 because of crossing traffic in the opposite direction.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Departure, Cathay 251, UNABLE to expedite, maximum climb rate 800 feet per minute.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot declares unable to expedite, stating a maximum climb rate of 800 fpm at heavy weight.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, roger, turn left immediately heading zero six zero for traffic avoidance.
exchanges.meaning: ATC acknowledges and issues a left turn to heading 060 for traffic avoidance.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Turn left heading zero six zero, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback of the traffic-avoidance turn.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, climb via SID to Flight Level zero nine zero.
exchanges.meaning: The pure taught form of the climb-via-SID clearance: follow the published lateral route and all altitude/speed constraints up to FL090.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, cancel level restriction, climb to Flight Level one six zero.
exchanges.meaning: The pure taught form cancelling published step-climb caps for an unrestricted climb to FL160.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Climb to Flight Level one six zero, cancel level restriction, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pure taught readback of the unrestricted climb with the restriction cancellation.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, STOP CLIMB at Flight Level one two zero!
exchanges.meaning: The pure taught emergency command to arrest the climb immediately at FL120.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, expedite climb through Flight Level one zero zero.
exchanges.meaning: The pure taught command to increase vertical speed through FL100.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Expediting through Flight Level one zero zero, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback confirming the expedited climb through FL100.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, unable to expedite, maximum vertical speed 800 feet per minute.
exchanges.meaning: The mandatory pilot response when the aircraft cannot climb faster; aerodynamic safety is never sacrificed for an expedite request.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, NEGATIVE! STOP CLIMB IMMEDIATELY at Flight Level one two zero!
exchanges.meaning: The mandatory ATC correction after the pilot read back 'climbing to FL120' instead of 'stopping climb at FL120'.

vocabulary.definition: Standard Instrument Departure — a published 3D departure route with lateral track and waypoint altitude/speed constraints.
A clearance legally binding the pilot to follow the SID's lateral track and comply with all published waypoint altitude and speed constraints up to the cleared level.
A published waypoint crossing constraint on a SID (e.g. 'cross BEKOL at or below 5,000 ft') protecting terrain clearance and airspace segregation.
An urgent ATC command to immediately arrest the climb and level off at the assigned flight level, used for unexpected overhead traffic conflicts.
An ATC command to increase vertical speed to the maximum safe rate through a flight level.
The autopilot vertical mode (Level Change) used after 'cancel level restriction' to climb unrestricted at maximum climb thrust to the assigned level.

quiz.question: [Question 1 — Air Law & Radiotelephony (ICAO Doc 4444)] When an air traffic controller issues the clearance: "Cathay 251, climb via SID to Flight Level 100", what is the pilot authorized and required to do?
options: Climb unrestricted directly to FL100, disregarding all published SID waypoint altitude constraints.
Follow the lateral track of the SID, comply with all published waypoint altitude and speed constraints on the chart, and climb up to FL100.
Maintain runway heading until reaching 3,000 feet, then turn direct to the first waypoint.
Maintain minimum clean speed and request radar vectors.
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO Doc 4444 Amendment 7, 'CLIMB VIA SID' legally binds the pilot to the lateral track AND all published vertical and speed constraints up to the cleared level.

quiz.question: [Question 2 — Principles of Flight & Aircraft Performance] How do an increase in aircraft gross weight and high density altitude affect an aircraft's Rate of Climb (ROC) and Angle of Climb (AOC)?
options: Both Rate of Climb and Angle of Climb are reduced.
Rate of Climb increases, but Angle of Climb decreases.
Angle of Climb increases, but Rate of Climb remains unchanged.
Both Rate of Climb and Angle of Climb are improved due to increased inertia.
quiz.explanation: Higher weight creates more induced drag and reduces excess thrust; high density altitude degrades engine power — since climb depends on excess power (ROC) and excess thrust (AOC), both are reduced.

sections.heading: Core Learning Content — Sid Climb Phraseology
sections.body: Per ICAO Doc 4444 (PANS-ATM) Amendment 7 and ICAO Doc 9432: (1) Climb via SID: ATC "Cathay 251, climb via SID to Flight Level zero nine zero." → readback "Climb via SID to Flight Level zero nine zero, Cathay 251." Meaning: follow the published lateral route AND comply with all published altitude crossing limits and speed restrictions up to FL090. (2) Cancelling constraints: ATC "Cathay 251, cancel level restriction, climb to Flight Level one six zero." → readback "Climb to Flight Level one six zero, cancel level restriction, Cathay 251." Meaning: ignore all published step-climb caps; climb unrestricted straight to FL160. (3) Emergency level-off: ATC "Cathay 251, STOP CLIMB at Flight Level one two zero!" → readback "Stopping climb at Flight Level one two zero, Cathay 251." (4) Expedite: ATC "Cathay 251, expedite climb through Flight Level one zero zero." → readback "Expediting through Flight Level one zero zero, Cathay 251." If unable: "Cathay 251, unable to expedite, maximum vertical speed 800 feet per minute."

sections.heading: Spaced Repetition (Forgetting Curve) Review
sections.body: Day 9 & 11 recall — (1) Initial check-in sequence: Station → Callsign → PASSING [Current Altitude] → CLIMBING TO [Assigned Level] → [SID]. (2) Passing altitude is reported so the controller can verify Mode C telemetry matches the cockpit altimeter within ±200 feet. (3) Takeoff Taboo: the word "takeoff" is reserved for takeoff clearance or cancellation; at the holding point always say "ready for DEPARTURE".

sections.heading: Fun Aviation Fact Of The Day
sections.body: The "Expedite" trap and heavy jet aerodynamics: in a fully loaded airliner climbing at high altitude on a warm day, the aircraft operates near its performance ceiling ("Coffin Corner") — pitching up to climb faster trades airspeed for altitude, and speed can decay toward an unrecoverable high-altitude stall. ICAO procedures explicitly instruct pilots to reply "UNABLE to expedite" whenever performance or safety margins would be compromised.
